very useful why because it is a 136 page home office report that tracked 3527 service users and complainants across six study sites in england the data was collected roughly from 2000 to 2002 and for the part we care about false allegations the study looks at 2643 cases that were reported to police so again not perfect but probably one of the best if not the best study on this topic out there and the first thing that truly surprised me is how many cases never even reach court in this study only 14 percent of reported cases reached the trial stage meaning if 100 women reported to police that they were raped only around 14 cases eventually reached trial around 86 didn't that is pretty crazy and this is what researchers call attrition attrition basically means cases dropping out of the criminal justice process and the study tries to understand why this happens but even there it is not that simple because yes we have police categories like insufficient evidence victim withdrawal victim declined to complete the initial process offender not identified false allegation no evidence of assault no prospect of conviction and other reasons but these categories do not always fully explain what actually happened underneath for example victim withdrawal can mean many different things maybe the person was afraid of court maybe she didn't want family or friends to find out maybe she didn't trust the police maybe the process was too traumatic maybe the evidence was weak maybe she changed her mind and yes in some cases maybe the allegation was false but you cannot just look at withdrawal and say ha false allegation same with insufficient evidence that doesn't mean nothing happened it means the case didn't have enough evidence to move forward and this is where the topic becomes even messier because a case can be true and still not go to court a case can go to court and still not lead to conviction and the case can be false and never reach court at all so before we even talk about false allegation percentages we need to understand one thing the justice system doesn't divide cases neatly into true and false a lot of cases end up in this uncomfortable middle
